about.title: Santa Clarita Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Clarita is home to about 182,000 people, and the public record shows how often its roads see collisions. In 2025, the city logged 706 injury collisions, with 1,042 people hurt and 14 lives lost. Counts run highest on Soledad Canyon Road, Sierra Highway, Bouquet Canyon Road and McBean Parkway, and reports cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If one of those numbers now describes your week, the practical steps matter more than the statistics. See a doctor even if you feel fine, photograph the vehicles and the scene, keep every receipt, and hold off on giving the other driver's insurer a recorded statement until you have had legal advice. California gives you two years to file a claim in most cases, but only six months if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect people in Santa Clarita with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Clarita Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than Most People Think
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident claim, but a crash involving a city, county or state vehicle or road issue can shrink that window to six months. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to you.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for the collision; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. Insurers sometimes use fault arguments to discourage valid claims.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, so you pay nothing up front and nothing at all if there is no recovery. Our connection service is free as well.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster keeps calling me. Should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: It is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Recorded statements are often taken while you are still sorting out your injuries, and a casual remark can later be used to lower your claim. You can politely say you are not ready and will be in touch.

items.question: My crash was on Sierra Highway near a Caltrans work zone. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. If a government entity's road design, signage or maintenance played a role, California requires you to file an administrative claim within six months rather than the usual two years. Because that deadline arrives quickly, it is worth getting your situation reviewed soon.

items.question: Does California limit how much I can recover for pain and suffering after a car accident?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life in car accident cases. The value of your claim depends on your specific injuries, treatment and how the crash affected your daily life, which an attorney can evaluate with you.
